name: Real Option Qualification Gate

positioning.oneLineSummary: Allows a separate option value only when there is incremental optionality, exclusivity, a finite window, an exercise cost, and no DCF double count.
positioning.productLabel: Real Option Gate — based on Aswath Damodaran's public real-option materials
notAClaimOf: management flexibility automatically creating option value
growth already in a DCF deserving an extra premium

attribution.display: Based on Aswath Damodaran's public real-option materials

neutralParaphrase: A strategic opportunity resembles a real option only when a current asset or investment creates an incremental right to delay, expand, abandon, or develop; the company has meaningful exclusivity or competitive advantage; the right has a finite useful life; exercise requires an identifiable investment; uncertainty can increase the upside; and the same cash flows are not already counted in the base valuation.

locator.value: PDF pp. 24-31 and 51-53: delay/expansion options, exclusivity, term, erosion, estimation limitations, and competitive advantage
PDF pp. 61-64: selective real-option application, exclusivity, time limits, and double-counting constraints

requiredConditions: The optional future cash flow is incremental to the base valuation.
A legal, technological, contractual, network, or structural source of exclusivity is identified.
The exercise decision, exercise cost, option window, and expiration or erosion mechanism are defined.
The option model assumptions can be estimated with ranges and are not copied from traded stock volatility.

requiredEvidence.description: Specific incremental project or market cash flows and the current asset that creates access.
Evidence that competitors cannot exercise the same opportunity on equivalent terms during the option window.
Exercise cost, time to expiration, erosion, delay cost, abandonment value, and decision trigger.
Line-by-line proof that the option's cash flows are absent from base revenue, margin, reinvestment, and terminal value.

decisionQuestions: What present asset or investment creates the future right?
What incremental cash flows are excluded from the base DCF?
Why can the company, but not an equivalent rival, exercise the opportunity?
What are the exercise cost, decision trigger, term, and erosion mechanism?
Is uncertainty about the underlying value measurable without false precision?
Would removing the separate option leave any of its growth inside terminal value?
positiveSignals: The company holds verifiable exclusive rights for a finite period.
Management can wait for information before committing the exercise cost.
The opportunity has identifiable incremental cash flows and decision triggers.
Competitive entry and erosion are explicitly modeled.
A reconciliation proves no overlap with base DCF.
redFlags: The option is described only as a large TAM or future possibility.
Competitors can enter on equal terms.
No exercise cost, term, or decision point exists.
Volatility is copied from public stock returns without connection to project value.
The same expansion appears in revenue forecasts or terminal value.
disconfirmingEvidence: Rights expire before technical or commercial readiness.
Competition can enter sooner than the option window assumes.
The opportunity requires irreversible investment before uncertainty resolves.
Base DCF already includes the market expansion.
Reasonable input ranges make option value immaterial or indeterminate.
contraindications: Do not apply option pricing to generic managerial flexibility.
Do not add a real-option premium without exclusivity.
Do not double count forecast or terminal growth.
Do not let the LLM estimate option value or volatility.

instructions: Identify the incremental opportunity and current access asset.
Run exclusivity, finite-term, exercise-cost, and information-arrival gates.
Reconcile option cash flows against the base valuation.
If every gate passes, send bounded inputs to the deterministic option service.
Otherwise classify the item as strategic upside, scenario variation, or not applicable without separate value.

sourceReliability.low: The opportunity is only a management narrative.
sourceReliability.medium: Project and market evidence exist but exclusivity or term is incomplete.
sourceReliability.high: Rights, project economics, term, exercise cost, competition, and base-model reconciliation are verified.

evidenceStrength.medium: Most option gates pass but one material input relies on a broad range.
evidenceStrength.high: All gates pass with independent legal, technical, commercial, and financial evidence.

evidenceCoverage.low: Only TAM and future possibility are covered.
evidenceCoverage.medium: Underlying, rights, and cost are covered but erosion or double count is incomplete.
evidenceCoverage.high: Underlying, exclusivity, term, exercise, uncertainty, competition, and reconciliation are covered.

applicabilityConfidence.low: The opportunity is shared or already in the base case.
applicabilityConfidence.medium: The opportunity resembles an option but exclusivity is time-uncertain.
applicabilityConfidence.high: The opportunity has a clear company-specific option structure.

judgmentConfidence.low: No separate option value is supportable.
judgmentConfidence.medium: A bounded option range may be calculated with important caveats.
judgmentConfidence.high: A deterministic option calculation is supported and separately reconciled.

promotionRequirements: Complete lawful third-edition and real-option chapter review.
Validate gate precision and recall on expert-labeled cases.
Review deterministic option-model assumptions by sector.
empiricalQualifications: Project-value volatility and option life are difficult to estimate.
Competitive entry can erase practical exclusivity faster than legal terms suggest.
Many strategic opportunities are better represented as scenarios than separate options.

rights.notes: Public real-option doctrine is neutrally paraphrased.

openIssues: Define deterministic model choices and input-quality floors by option type.
